Vehicle & Traffic Route Optimization Architecture

02 / FORMULATION

Traffic-aware CVRPTW

The benchmark minimizes travel time while enforcing capacity, time windows, flow conservation, depot, and subtour constraints.

01 / PROBLEM DEFINITION

Traffic-Aware Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows

The transportation network is a directed graph. The optimizer determines routes that visit every customer exactly once, respect capacity and time windows, originate and terminate at the depot, and minimize traffic-aware routing cost.

G=(V,E)
V set of nodesE directed road segments0 depot nodeVᶜ = V ∖ {0} customer nodesK vehicle setqᵢ, sᵢ, [aᵢ,bᵢ] demand, service time, window
02 / SETS & PARAMETERS

Inputs to the model

V=nodes,E=directed edges,Vc=V∖{0},K=vehicles
  • qᵢ demand; Qₖ vehicle capacity
  • sᵢ service time; [aᵢ,bᵢ] time window
  • Dᵢⱼ distance; τ⁰ᵢⱼ base travel time
03 / DECISION VARIABLES

What the optimizer chooses

xijk∈{0,1}

xᵢⱼₖ = 1 if vehicle k travels from i to j; otherwise 0.

tik=departure time from node ik,yik∈{0,1}

yᵢₖ = 1 assigns customer i to vehicle k.

04 / DYNAMIC TRAFFIC MODEL

Departure time changes the edge cost

CONGESTION LEVEL
Cij(t)=clip(Bij+Aijsin(2πtT+φij),0,Cmax)
TIME-DEPENDENT TRAVEL TIME
τij(t)=τ0ij(1+αCij(t))

Bᵢⱼ baseline, Aᵢⱼ amplitude, T period, φᵢⱼ phase, and Cₘₐₓ upper bound. The deterministic model uses τᵢⱼ = τᵢⱼ(t), not a fixed edge weight.

05 / OBJECTIVE FUNCTION

Travel time is the primary criterion

minZ=∑k∈K∑i∈V∑j∈Vxijk[wtτij(tik)+wdDij+wcCij(tik)]
wt=1,wd=0,wc=0

Travel time is optimized in the primary benchmark. Distance and congestion remain available as diagnostic metrics, not simultaneous primary objectives.

06 / CUSTOMER VISIT

Every customer exactly once

∑k∈K∑j∈Vxijk=1,∀i∈Vc
07 / FLOW CONSERVATION

Vehicles do not disappear

∑j∈Vxijk=∑j∈Vxjik,∀i∈Vc,k∈K
08 / CAPACITY

Demand stays within fleet limits

∑i∈Vcqiyik≤Qk,∀k∈K
09 / TIME WINDOWS

Service respects availability

ai≤tik≤bi,∀i∈Vc,k∈K
10 / TEMPORAL PROPAGATION

Earlier traffic changes later departures

tjk≥tik+si+τij(tik)−M(1−xijk)

M is sufficiently large. For route (v₀, v₁, …, vₘ), time is propagated sequentially: an earlier congested edge changes the departure time and conditions of every subsequent edge.

11 / DEPOT & ROUTES

Origin and return at node 0

∑j∈Vcx0jk≤1,∑i∈Vcxi0k≤1

Each vehicle can depart from and return to the single depot at most once.

12 / SUBTOUR HANDLING

Decoder-level structural feasibility

Subtour prevention is handled procedurally by the route decoder/evaluator: random keys are sorted into a permutation, then split into capacity-aware routes with depot closure. No unimplemented MILP/MTZ constraint is claimed here.

13 / PENALIZED EVALUATION FUNCTION

Infeasibility is visible in the score

F=Z+λQVQ+λTVT+λRVR

VQ, VT, and VR measure capacity, time-window, and routing/structural violation; λ terms are penalty coefficients. Feasibility is VQ = VT = VR = 0. Candidates are scored rather than silently discarded.

14 / COMMON EVALUATOR

Fair benchmark interface

AlgorithmCandidate routeDecoderTraffic-aware evaluatorFitness

The same objective, constraints, penalties, instances, scenarios, and evaluation budget are used for QPSO, PSO, GA, ALNS, and Random Search.
